name: The Liberty
positioning: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston: the former Charles Street Jail, a national historic landmark from 1851, transformed into a hotel at the foot of Beacon Hill
best_for: Travelers who love historic architecture and adaptive reuse
Visitors who want a Beacon Hill base by Charles Street and the Esplanade

facts.text: The hotel is a transformation of the former Charles Street Jail, a national historic landmark built in 1851.
The hotel is located at the foot of Beacon Hill.
The Charles Street Jail was a collaboration between architect Gridley James Fox Bryant and Rev. Louis Dwight, an advocate of prison reform.
The building has an octagonal central building with four radiating wings, each with large three-story arched windows.
The cupola was rebuilt based on Bryant's original design.
Exposed brick walls and a wrought iron chandelier feature in the lobby.
A 16-story tower houses guest rooms, many with expansive views of Boston.
Most rooms feature floor-to-ceiling windows, and many have views of the Charles River.
Preserved jail cell facades are part of CLINK., the hotel's signature restaurant.
Guests also have access to Equinox on Avery St.
Boat and kayak rentals can be arranged at the front desk.

highlights.text: The Ebersol Suite offers a 270-degree panoramic view of Boston, from the State House around to Charlestown, which can also be enjoyed from its open-air patio.
The jail's former exercise yard is now a private, landscaped courtyard.
Many accommodations feature private balconies with views of Beacon Hill and the Charles River.
The Liberty Bar is set in the hotel's 90-foot rotunda lobby.
Historic Charles Street, with its shops and boutiques, is directly across from the hotel, and the Esplanade is steps away.

considerations.text: The minimum age to check in is 21.
The hotel charges a nightly destination fee.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have smaller room sizes.
